20.en: "One glorious day, the God-Emperor Himself will lead us into a new age."

38.en: The God-Emperor’s spirit wanders the Warp, occasionally manifesting when His people truly need Him, in chosen vessels that can only contain a sliver of his power.

46.en: One day, He will return and require a Divine Avatar or vessel to inhabit.

54.en: Seeking out these vessels or means to implement them will hasten His return.

76.en: Seek out pure vessels for the God-Emperor’s eventual return or the means to create one. Investigate signs of the Emperor’s divinity throughout the sector, and seek for ways to guide or transfer His soul from the Warp to realspace.

82.en: For Thorians, the Emperor travels in spirit through the void and the Warp. He has already moved among the populace, granting an element of his divinity to various saints over the years. Still, Thorians believe that one day, He will inhabit a vessel that can contain Him in His entirety. Thorians, therefore, seek a suitable Divine Avatar to contain His spirit. This avatar must be exceptionally pure since a corrupt vessel might merely use the Emperor’s power for diabolical ends.

86.en: The Thorians’ philosophy is named for Sebastian Thor, who overthrew a High Lord of Terra’s tyrannous rule and ended theAge of Apostasy. Thorians believe that the Emperor worked through Thor Himself and has lent his power to other great mortals since, including Lord Solar Macharius. Some believe this means the next avatar will be found in the Macharian Sector.

90.en: Thorians investigate potential avatars and destroy those deemed unworthy. There are plenty of psykers, fortunetellers, and supposed ‘saints’ in the Macharian Sector, and an Inquisitor could spend a lifetime searching in just one hive. However, some might instead devote their time to their secondary task, learning to transfer consciousness to and from the Warp so that they might guide the God-Emperor to a new vessel.

94.en: Some Inquisitors think the Thorians misguided, but the @UUID[.R7LueEsDUhrSYHNn]{Amalathians} consider them dangerous, as putting faith in some powerful mortal would threaten the rule of the real God-Emperor on His Golden Throne. @UUID[.vJmDVccuyJJLooV4]{Polypsykana} Inquisitors object to Thorians’ tendency to destroy the many psykers they find unworthy, while @UUID[.2uYpfwwAdPf6e21L]{Oblationists} call their experiments heretical.

110.en: Despite its wild claims about the God-Emperor’s divinity, the Thorian philosophy is still considered Puritan. Its Inquisitors strive for purity and truth in the vessels they chase and are more willing to admit they have found yet another failure than trick themselves into ill-gotten beliefs — their standards are impossibly high and exacting.

118.en: Yet Thorians are often headstrong and singular in vision; many ignore the idea that if the God-Emperor returned as they envision, it would cause a civil war across the Imperium that could rival the Horus Heresy.

126.en: Regardless of their keen interest in the Warp and psychic abilities, Thorian Inquisitors will not suffer the influence of any daemon nor any psyker who exhibits corruptive behaviour.

140.en: A recent skirmish near the @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.1AsBzkbw2InKayw2]{Ayzinith Abyss} has left a voidship graveyard in its wake, wreckage from both Aeldari and Imperial vessels floating in the void. Investigate the Aeldari wreckage under the guise of an Inquisitorial cleanup — their technology is said to have the power to manipulate psychic energies and capture souls; it could prove fruitful in the Patron’s research.

148.en: The Thorian Inquisitor is concerned about a missing noble, Fentessa, daughter of Barius Perrore, governor of @UUID[Compendium.navis-apexialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.B7MZBBT3bNew9N96.JournalEntryPage.A9cvKlA41X8qPyEw]{Paleon}. Rumours say Fentessa has an uncanny way of knowing people’s secrets, and local officials are relieved she has disappeared. Her absence has caused unrest among Paleon’s lowborn, with whom she was inexplicably popular — even revered.
